questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Poland?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Poland article.

questions.proof: Most Polish people live in large cities, including the capital, Warsaw, Łódź, Cracow, the second capital of Poland (first was Gniezno), Szczecin, Gdańsk, Wrocław and Poznań.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Poland?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Poland on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Poland article.

questions.proof: The Czech Republic and Slovakia are to the south, Ukraine and Belarus to the east, and the Baltic Sea, Lithuania, and the Russian exclave of Kaliningrad to the north.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Poland?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Literature” part of the Poland article.

questions.proof: Polish literature was written in the Latin language during the Middle Ages.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “The total land area of Poland is about 312,679 km2 (120,728 mi2), slightly larger than _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “larger”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Poland article.

questions.proof: The total land area of Poland is about 312,679 km2 (120,728 mi2), slightly larger than Oman.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “However, Poland lost independence again not long after the beginning of World War II, after suffering a defeat by both the Soviet Union and Nazi _____.”

hints.nudge: In the sentence the missing word sits beside “Nazi”. It names one thing, not an action.
hints.whereToLook: It is further down the Poland article, under the heading “World War II”.

questions.proof: Poland divided into one part ruled by Nazi Germany and the other by the Soviet Union.
